items.title: How many bets can this team actually run in parallel?
items.description: L2's inputs list included 'org capacity,' but neither proposal put a number on it. Splitting a fixed 40-engineer team across more simultaneous bets doesn't just divide capacity evenly — each additional parallel bet adds coordination and context-switching overhead that eats into everyone's output. Drag the number of parallel bets up and watch effective delivery capacity fall faster than a simple split would predict.

params.name: parallelBets
params.label: Number of bets run in parallel

items.compute: const overheadPerExtraBet = 0.12; const switchingLoss = Math.min(0.7, (params.parallelBets - 1) * overheadPerExtraBet); const effectiveEngineers = Math.round(params.teamSize * (1 - switchingLoss)); const perBetCapacity = Math.round(effectiveEngineers / params.parallelBets); return { effectiveEngineers, perBetCapacity };

items.title: How much rework does skipping dependency order really cost?
items.description: L3's chart showed billing-before-split adding an estimated 14 engineer-weeks of rework. That number isn't fixed — it scales with how much of billing's code touches the monolith's data-access layer directly. Drag how tightly coupled billing is to the monolith, and how many quarters pass before the split eventually happens anyway, to see how the rework cost of ignoring dependency order grows.

params.name: couplingPercent
params.label: % of billing code coupled to monolith internals

params.name: quartersDeferred
params.label: Quarters the split is deferred after billing ships

items.compute: const baseBillingWeeks = 36; const couplingFraction = params.couplingPercent / 100; const driftPerQuarter = 0.06; const driftMultiplier = 1 + params.quartersDeferred * driftPerQuarter; const reworkWeeks = Math.round(baseBillingWeeks * couplingFraction * driftMultiplier * 0.5); return { reworkWeeks };
